sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Interesting! After LEFT + SPACE:
- Frame is now diamond-shaped (id=11, 43 pixels, boundary shows diamond corners)
- Frame fill (id=12) is purple, 85 pixels, also diamond-shaped
- Block top (id=13) is purple, 65 pixels - it grew from 50 to 65 pixels! The boundary changed from [[34,27],[34,36],[38,36],[38,27]] to [[34,27],[34,36],[38,36],[38,32]] - the left edge moved from col 27 to col 32
- Block bottom (id=14) is white, 35 pixels - shrank from 50 to 35 pixels. Boundary changed from [[39,27],[39,36],[43,36],[43,27]] to [[39,32],[39,36],[43,36],[43,28]]
So SPACE with the diamond frame changed the block's shape! The purple portion expanded to the left (more pixels) and the white portion shrank. The block now has a diagonal/l-shaped boundary between purple and white.
This suggests SPACE "stamps" the frame's shape onto the block. With a rectangular frame, it creates a horizontal split. With a diamond frame, it creates a diagonal split.
Let me think about this differently. Maybe the game is about "painting" the block with different shapes to create a specific pattern. The palette shows white-over-purple (horizontal split). The current block has a diagonal purple/white split.
Let me try RIGHT to restore the rectangular frame, then SPACE again to see if it resets to horizontal split.
